question: Which among the following is the largest unit of memory?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Petabyte**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **largest unit of memory** is **Petabyte**.
 
• **Petabyte (PB)** is the largest unit, representing massive amounts of data storage typically used in fields like data centers, cloud storage, and large-scale computing environments.
 
• A **petabyte is a measure of memory or data storage capacity that is equal to 2 to the 50th power of bytes.**
 
• A **petabyte is 1,000 times larger than a terabyte **

 [IMAGE: https://teach-ict.com/2016/images/diagrams/data_sizes.jpg] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Byte**: The basic unit of digital information storage.
 
• **Kilobyte (KB)**: 1 Kilobyte = 1,024 Bytes.
 
• **Megabyte (MB)**: 1 Megabyte = 1,024 Kilobytes.
 
• **Gigabyte (GB)**: 1 Gigabyte = 1,024 Megabytes.
 
• **Terabyte (TB)**: 1 Terabyte = 1,024 Gigabytes.
